title: Golf Gifts for the Golfer Who Has Everything, Plus Ike at Augusta
excerpt: Golf gifts for the golfer who has everything: Gift a Season of Mully Reserve, three gifts to wrap, and how Eisenhower spent Thanksgiving at Augusta National.

intro: Gift a Season for the golfer who already owns everything, three gifts to wrap, and the Thanksgivings President Eisenhower spent at Augusta National.
highlights: Gift a Season: a Mully stylist picks his pieces every season. It's one-time and prepaid, and it never renews.
Three gifts to wrap: an Olydoe merino quarter zip, a Duck Head quilted vest and a Rhone knit polo.
Through the 1950s, President Eisenhower spent Thanksgiving at Augusta National, and carved the turkey in 1954.

sections.heading: The gift that keeps showing up
paragraphs: For the golfer who already owns the putter, the rangefinder and three of every polo.
Some golfers are impossible to shop for. So don't give him a thing. Give him a season.

Every season a Mully stylist picks a few pieces for him: apparel and accessories, in his sizes, including a few he might not have picked himself. You choose his usual sizes when you order, and he can update them before each season after that.
You pay once, and it never renews. It's a one-time, prepaid gift for one, two or four seasons, with no reveal to plan and nothing for him to cancel.
Most gifts get opened once. This one comes back every season. [Gift a Season](/lp/gift-season).

sections.heading: If you'd rather wrap something
paragraphs: Three gifts he'll wear all winter.

The one he'll wear to dinner too: the [Olydoe Merino Ponte Quarter Zip](/shop/olydoe-merino-ponte-quarter-zip) in Highland Green. Olydoe makes it from 100% Australian merino in a double ponte knit, two layers knitted together for drape and durability with natural stretch. The brand calls it just as good on the course as off it.

The one for cold mornings: the [Duck Head Fremont Quilted Vest](/shop/duckhead-fremont-sport-performance-quilted-vest-brandy-brown) in Brandy Brown. A quilted performance vest that keeps his core warm and his arms free. It works over a polo on the course or a flannel at home.

The one with the Johnny collar: the [Rhone Back Nine Knit Polo](/shop/rhone-back-nine-knit-polo) in Toasted Oat. A midweight jacquard knit that feels like something he's owned for years. The Johnny collar gives it a relaxed, retro look that works at the turn and at dinner.
More ideas by price in [the gift guide](/shop/gifts). Fabric details via [Olydoe](https://olydoe.com/products/merino-wool-quarter-zip-copy).

sections.heading: Thanksgiving at Augusta National
paragraphs: Through the 1950s, President Eisenhower spent his Thanksgivings at Augusta National.
The members gave him a gift of their own in 1953: a cabin by the 10th tee, built for the first family. The club still calls it Mamie's Cabin.
On Thanksgiving Day 1954 he played 18 holes in perfect weather, with Field Marshal Montgomery following along in a cart. Then he carved a 43-pound turkey for about 50 members in the trophy room.

Not every gift went his way. Ike lobbied the club to cut down the loblolly pine on 17 that kept catching his tee shots. Clifford Roberts adjourned the meeting instead, and it stood as the Eisenhower Tree until an ice storm took it in 2014.

Sources: [Augusta Chronicle](https://www.augustachronicle.com/story/news/2016/11/23/way-we-were-eisenhower-frequent-thanksgiving-visitor/14275887007/), [White House Historical Association](https://www.whitehousehistory.org/press-room/press-timelines/thanksgiving-at-the-white-house), [The New York Times, 1954](https://www.nytimes.com/1954/11/26/archives/president-carves-43pound-turkey-dines-with-montgomery-after-playing.html), [Golf Monthly](https://www.golfmonthly.com/tour/augusta-national-facts). sections.heading: What's the best golf gift you've ever gotten?
paragraphs: A lesson from your dad, a round at a course you'd never get on, a putter you still use. Get the Mully Letter, reply to any issue, and tell us about it. A few sentences is plenty.
We read every one. If we'd like to share yours in an upcoming issue, we'll ask you first.
